by_task.when: Federal exemptions are an allowable namespace and the facts establish the debtor's ownership of an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Test 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) independently for every such asset because it covers any property. Include it alongside every matching category-specific exemption; its dollar limit restricts value, not EC eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it when Federal is not allowable or ownership is not established, and do not list § 522(b), § 522(d), or § 522(m) as asset exemptions.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and the facts establish the debtor's ownership and value of an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Report 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) once as an independent alternative alongside every matching category-specific exemption. Evaluate that alternative without allocating exemptions to other assets: claim the lesser of the asset value and $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of § 522(d)(1) unused in that alternative. In a joint case, § 522(m) applies this calculation separately to each spouse's interest, permitting up to $30,850 total for jointly owned property.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it when Federal is not allowable or ownership is not established, do not subtract claims made under separate asset-exemption alternatives, and do not report § 522(m), § 522(b), or § 522(d) as an asset exemption.

operations.rationale: In these seen EV cases, the parent repeatedly returned category-specific federal exemptions but omitted § 522(d)(5), although the released targets include it independently for owned vehicles, trade tools, residences, household goods, apparel, jewelry, and musical instruments. The existing EC rule already states the correct eligibility boundary and is retained verbatim; the added EV block supplies only the missing independent amount calculation, joint-debtor treatment, and non-exemption citation exclusions. Unlike the rejected ALL-jurisdiction proposal, this edit is confined to the Federal namespace and instructs the actor to report the alternative only once.
